tools.name: list-aem-environments
tools.title: List AEM Environments
tools.description: Discover the AEM environments the current user can access with their credentials — no aemUrl or other parameters required. Run this first when you don't yet have a target environment URL, or when switching environments. Typical workflow: list-aem-environments → pick an environment → use its authorUrl with lookup-api-spec / read-api / write-api.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous call's nextCursor. Omit to get the first page.

limit.description: Maximum environments to return per page (default 20, max 100).

text.description: Human-readable summary of the AEM environments the current user can access.

environments.description: The accessible AEM environments. Use an environment's authorUrl as the `aemUrl` parameter for lookup-api-spec/read-api/write-api/delete-api. Not all tier URLs are present for every environment.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `cursor` on the next call to retrieve more environments. Absent when there are no more.

tools.name: lookup-api-spec
tools.title: Lookup AEM API Spec & Recipes
tools.description:
Discover AEM API endpoints, recipes, and skills by writing JavaScript — for a task or domain concept (e.g. "brand guidelines", "governance checks"), search skills/recipes, not just endpoints.
Runs in a sandbox with read-only `spec`, `recipes`, and `featureFlags` objects.
**All methods are async — you MUST `await` every call** (they resolve over the capabilities service).

**Workflow awareness** (check BEFORE writing code):
- CF-FIRST: Pages/Sites are containers — most content lives in Content Fragments. Read page content to find CF paths, resolve to UUIDs, then use the CF API.
- LAUNCH MODE: Before editing content, check for active launches — edits may need to target launch copies, not production.
- ETAG: ALL mutations require GET-first for ETag. Retry on 412.
- ASYNC JOBS: Launch create/promote/rebase/diff return 202. Poll job status.
- FORM ENCODING: /bin/* endpoints require aem.form(), NOT aem.post().
Use `await spec.workflows()` to list all workflows, `await spec.workflow('id')` for full procedures.

**Getting started:** Use `await spec.capabilities()` to see what AEM can do, then `await spec.capability('id')` to get endpoints + workflows for a specific capability.

**Common starting points:**
- `return await spec.capabilities();` — list all AEM capabilities (recommended first call)
- `return await spec.capability('page-content');` — endpoints + workflows for page editing
- `return await spec.capability('fragment-management');` — content fragment CRUD
- `return await spec.capability('launches');` — launches & scheduled publishing
- `return await spec.capability('feature-flags');` — feature flags (Adobe employees only)
- `return await recipes.search('update component');` — tree navigation + JSON Patch patterns

**`spec` methods** (all async — must `await`):
- `await spec.capabilities()` — list all capabilities (intent → endpoints + workflows)
- `await spec.capability(id)` — get one capability with primary endpoints, workflows, and recipes
- `await spec.workflows()` — list cross-cutting workflow patterns (launch mode, ETag, async jobs, etc.)
- `await spec.workflow(id)` — full state machine with steps, quirks, and related items
- `await spec.search(query)` — find endpoints by short verb+noun query (e.g. "list pages", "delete page", "get launch sources"). Prefer verb+noun over bare nouns.
- `await spec.byGroup(group)` — filter by API group (for fine-grained lookup)
- `await spec.byTier(tier)` — filter by tier: author, publish, delivery
- `await spec.byPath(pattern)` — string or RegExp path matching
- `await spec.byMethod(method)` — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
- `await spec.byAnnotation(key, value)` — readOnly, destructive, requiresETag
- `await spec.detail(method, path)` — full OpenAPI detail for one endpoint
- `await spec.raw(method, path)` — full resolved OpenAPI operation (allOf/oneOf, nested schemas, property constraints)
- `await spec.listAll()` — one-line summary of every endpoint
- `await spec.stats` — group names and endpoint counts

- Provide `aemUrl` to auto-filter by tier (author/publish/delivery). Without it, all tiers are shown.

**Progressive disclosure:** Start with `await spec.capabilities()`, then `await spec.capability(id)` for workflows, then `await spec.detail('PATCH', '/path')` for full schema.

**Recommended traversal for practitioner-phrased intents, TASKS, or DOMAIN-CONCEPT queries** (e.g. "brand guidelines", "governance checks" — not just endpoint-shaped ones):
1. `await skills.search(intent)` — search by practitioner outcome (e.g. "add variation to fragment", "create launch for review", "brand guidelines")
2. `await skills.get(id)` — full skill detail: outcome, preconditions, UI path, ordered steps
3. Execute using `read-api` (reads), `write-api` (creates/updates/publication-state changes like unpublish), or `delete-api` (deletes and other destructive ops) with the listed recipes from `await skills.plan(id)`. A skill's own `Intent` (shown in `skills.get(id)`) tells you which tool to use.
Fall back to `await recipes.search()` for technical phrasings; raw `await spec.search()` is the last resort — it ONLY finds OpenAPI endpoints, so it returns nothing for capabilities that have none (e.g. brand-governance and other upstream-MCP-backed domains). If `spec.search`/`spec.capabilities()` comes up empty or irrelevant for a phrase like "list X guidelines/checks/policy", try `skills.search`/`recipes.search` on the same phrase before concluding the capability doesn't exist.

**`skills` methods** (all async — must `await`):
- `await skills.search(query)` — find skills by practitioner intent (e.g. "publish fragment", "add translation")
- `await skills.get(id)` — get full skill detail by slug (outcome, steps, preconditions, UI path)
- `await skills.list()` — compact list of all skills (id, name, capability, area, audience)
- `await skills.byCapability(capId)` — all skills under a capability
- `await skills.byArea(area)` — filter by area (fragments, pages, assets, translation, etc.)
- `await skills.plan(id)` — resolve skill steps to concrete Recipe objects for execution

**`recipes` methods** (all async — must `await`):
- `await recipes.search(query)` — find recipes by short verb+noun query (e.g. "list pages", "create launch", "publish content"). Avoid bare-noun queries — they match too many recipes.
  Tip: include the operation verb (list, create, update, delete, publish) AND the object — e.g. "list pages", "delete launch". One-word noun queries match too broadly.
- `await recipes.get(name)` — get a specific recipe by name
- `await recipes.list()` / `await recipes.listAll()` — list all recipes with parameters

**`featureFlags` methods** (code-mode feature flags):
- `featureFlags.list()` — list all code-mode feature flags with enabled status
- `featureFlags.get(flag)` — get a specific flag by ID
- `featureFlags.getEnabled()` — get currently enabled flag IDs

MUST use `return` to output results. ALL spec/skills/recipes methods return Promises — you MUST `await` them.
Example: `return await spec.capabilities();`
Example: `return await spec.search('list fragment');`
Example: `return await skills.search('publish fragment variation');`
Example: `return await skills.plan('my-skill-id');`
Example: `return await recipes.search('update component');`
Example with chaining: `const eps = await spec.search('page'); return eps.filter(e => e.method === 'GET');`

code.description: JavaScript code. Must use `return`. ALL spec/recipes/skills methods are async — you MUST `await` every call. For a task or domain concept (e.g. "asset metadata"), start with `skills.search(...)` or `recipes.search(...)`; `spec.search` finds OpenAPI endpoints ONLY and returns nothing for endpoint-less domains (e.g. some upstream-MCP-backed capabilities). Examples: `return await skills.search('asset metadata');`, `return await recipes.search('update page');`, `return await spec.search('list fragment');`

aemUrl.description: AEM environment URL. If provided, filters specs to endpoints available on that tier (author, publish, or delivery). Auto-detected from subdomain. A scheme (https://) is optional — a bare host (e.g. author-p1-e1.adobeaemcloud.com) is normalized automatically.

text.description: A formatted, human-readable list of matching AEM API endpoints, code recipes, and feature flags discovered by the sandbox code, including paths, summaries, and usage hints. Empty or 'no results' text means nothing matched the query.

tools.name: read-api
tools.title: Read AEM Content (Safe)
tools.description: Execute read-only AEM API calls (GET/HEAD only). ALWAYS call lookup-api-spec first — never guess endpoint paths.

code.description: Async JavaScript with `aem.get()` / `aem.head()` and/or `mcp.call()`. Must use `return`.

aemUrl.description: AEM environment URL. Required for AEM operations (aem.*). Not needed for upstream MCP calls (mcp.call), which resolve their endpoint server-side. Tier is auto-detected from subdomain. A scheme (https://) is optional — a bare host (e.g. author-p1-e1.adobeaemcloud.com) is normalized automatically.

text.description: The value returned by the sandboxed read code, serialized as text. For AEM reads this is typically JSON containing the response body (and ETag/status where applicable); for plain returns it is the string value. On failure it is an error message.

tools.name: write-api
tools.title: Write AEM Content (Validated)
tools.description: Execute AEM API mutations or flag management via sandboxed JavaScript. ALWAYS call lookup-api-spec first — never guess endpoint paths.

code.description: Async JavaScript with `aem` and/or `featureFlags` client calls. Must use `return`.

aemUrl.description: AEM environment URL. Required for AEM operations (aem.*). Not needed for feature flag management (featureFlags.*). Tier is auto-detected from subdomain. A scheme (https://) is optional — a bare host (e.g. author-p1-e1.adobeaemcloud.com) is normalized automatically.

text.description: An EXECUTED report describing the mutations that were applied. On failure it is an error message.

tools.name: delete-api
tools.title: Delete AEM Content (Requires Confirmation)
tools.description: Delete AEM content via sandboxed JavaScript. ALWAYS call lookup-api-spec first — never guess endpoint paths. IRREVERSIBLE — requires explicit confirmation.

code.description: Async JavaScript with `aem.get()` and `aem.delete()`. Must use `return`.

aemUrl.description: AEM environment URL (e.g., 'https://author-p12345-e67890.adobeaemcloud.com'). A scheme (https://) is optional — a bare host (e.g. author-p1-e1.adobeaemcloud.com) is normalized automatically.

text.description: A confirmation that the delete completed. On failure it is an error message.

tools.name: list-aem-capabilities
tools.title: List AEM capabilities
tools.description: ONLY for capability-discovery questions ("what can you do?", "what are your capabilities?", "help me get started", "what's possible"). NOT for task execution — if the user has a specific goal (list pages, search fragments, upload an asset, create a launch, etc.), use lookup-api-spec instead.

detail.description: 'summary' for capability headers + use-case names (default); 'full' for each use case's outcome statement

aemUrl.description: AEM environment URL. When provided, resolves the caller's feature-flag state so experimental (FT_-gated) capabilities/use-cases that are active show up in the normal listing. Omitted -> experimental capabilities/use-cases are hidden (fail closed); the Feedback Program section still lists them as available to try.

text.description: Markdown grouped by capability area (e.g. Content Fragments, Pages, Assets, Launches, Publishing, Templates, Search, Sites) describing practitioner-facing outcomes this AEM server supports. Detail level depends on the `detail` input.

detail.description: The detail level used to render the markdown.
